name: Expansion Thresholds
consequences: Accelerating suite expansion beyond 8 risks diluting data quality if staffing and annotation capacity cannot scale proportionally. Delaying expansion until 100% event capture rates may limit participant throughput but ensures robust validation of the residential model.
options: Trigger expansion at 80% event capture rates with parallel staffing increases
Delay expansion until 12-week stay completion rates exceed 90%
Implement modular renovations to convert non-sleep areas into temporary suites
review: Rushing expansion risks annotation bottlenecks and reduced event diversity, while overcautious thresholds may underutilize facility capacity and delay scientific output.

name: Recruitment Criteria Flexibility
consequences: Relaxing exclusion criteria could increase participant numbers but may introduce confounding variables like undiagnosed epilepsy. Strict adherence preserves data purity but risks enrollment shortfalls amid rare condition prevalence.
options: Allow controlled enrollment of participants with resolved substance use disorder
Create a tiered exclusion system with documented risk mitigation plans
Prioritize participants with documented family history of parasomnias
review: Loosening criteria risks clinical heterogeneity but improves recruitment viability, while maintaining strict exclusions may require alternative compensation strategies to attract participants.

name: Sensor Fusion Strategy
consequences: Adding biometric sensors increases data granularity but raises annotation complexity. Relying solely on existing sensors preserves workflow efficiency but may miss subtle physiological correlates of parasomnia transitions.
options: Integrate continuous blood pressure monitoring during sleep cycles
Deploy wearable ECG patches for cardiac rhythm correlation
Use ambient sound analysis to detect vocalization patterns
review: Expanding sensor arrays risks overwhelming annotation capacity without clear analytical frameworks, while limited sensing may fail to capture multi-modal event signatures.

name: Participant Incentive Structure
consequences: Tiered compensation based on event capture could motivate participation but may alter natural behavior through financial incentives. Fixed compensation ensures behavioral authenticity but may reduce retention rates during prolonged stays.
options: Offer bonus payments for participants contributing to event-triage algorithm training
Implement non-monetary incentives like personalized sleep reports
Create a loyalty-based compensation model with escalating rates for longer stays
review: Performance-based incentives risk introducing selection bias in event capture rates while fixed compensation may struggle to offset participant inconvenience costs.

name: Ethics Review Frequency
consequences: Semi-annual reviews ensure ongoing compliance but may delay adaptive changes. Annual reviews reduce administrative burden but increase risk of regulatory misalignment during rapid protocol iterations.
options: Implement real-time ethics monitoring for high-risk procedures
Create a subcommittee for expedited reviews of low-impact modifications
Adopt a pre-approved protocol change catalog for common adjustments
review: Frequent reviews enhance compliance but hinder agility, while infrequent reviews risk regulatory nonconformity during critical project phases.

name: Data Annotation Workflow
consequences: Implementing dual-rater consensus increases reliability but doubles annotation time. Single-rater workflows accelerate processing but introduce scorer bias risks, particularly for ambiguous events.
options: Train junior raters with senior oversight for high-volume nights
Use algorithmic pre-screening to flag ambiguous events for human review
Rotate raters monthly to reduce fatigue-induced variability
review: Dual-rater systems ensure consistency but strain annotation capacity, while single-rater approaches risk methodological inconsistencies without clear mitigation.

name: Public Data Sharing Scope
consequences: Expanding shared datasets increases scientific impact but heightens privacy risks. Limited sharing preserves confidentiality but restricts external validation opportunities and collaboration.
options: Release de-identified sensor metadata with video excerpts from non-participants
Create a restricted-access portal for approved researchers with data use agreements
Publish synthetic datasets generated through probabilistic modeling
review: Broader data sharing enhances reproducibility but requires robust anonymization protocols, while limited sharing may hinder methodological benchmarking against external datasets.

name: Staffing Rotation Models
consequences: Shifting to a 12-hour shift model reduces staff fatigue but increases total headcount requirements. This could strain budget constraints unless paired with cross-training to maintain coverage during peak event capture windows.
options: Implement a 12-hour shift model with staggered coverage
Introduce cross-training for staff to handle multiple roles
Adopt a rotating 3-shift schedule with mandatory rest periods
review: A 12-hour shift model reduces fatigue but increases staffing costs, requiring a trade-off between operational efficiency and budget constraints.

name: Safety Protocol Intensity
consequences: Adding real-time biometric monitoring for staff alertness improves incident response but creates dependency on technology that could fail during critical moments. This risks undermining manual oversight capabilities.
options: Integrate real-time biometric monitoring for staff alertness
Deploy redundant safety systems with automatic fail-safes
Conduct monthly safety drills with participant involvement
review: Enhanced safety systems improve incident response but risk over-reliance on technology, potentially undermining manual oversight during system failures.

name: Participant Retention Strategies
consequences: Offering tiered compensation based on event capture rates could increase productivity but might incentivize participants to manipulate sleep patterns, compromising naturalistic data integrity.
options: Create a performance-based bonus structure for event capture
Establish peer support networks among participants
Implement flexible stay extensions with reduced compensation
review: Performance-based incentives risk altering natural sleep behaviors, creating a conflict between data authenticity and participant motivation.

name: Emergency Response Protocols
consequences: Adding on-site medical personnel for acute episodes increases safety but requires additional training and certification, potentially delaying deployment if staffing shortages occur.
options: Train existing technicians in advanced emergency care
Establish direct ambulance response agreements with local hospitals
Install automated defibrillators with staff certification requirements
review: On-site medical staff improve immediate care but create dependency on specialized training that may not scale with facility expansion.

name: Equipment Maintenance Schedules
consequences: Implementing daily calibration routines for sensors increases data reliability but reduces available time for participant interactions and manual annotations.
options: Schedule maintenance during low-activity hours
Develop self-calibrating sensor arrays
Create a rotating maintenance shift for technical staff
review: Daily calibration improves data accuracy but competes with core research activities, creating a resource allocation dilemma.

name: Community Engagement Frameworks
consequences: Establishing neighborhood liaison programs could improve local acceptance but might introduce regulatory complexities if residents request access to facility data.
options: Create a local advisory board for facility operations
Host public education nights about sleep research
Develop a volunteer participant recruitment network
review: Community engagement builds goodwill but risks uncontrolled data access requests that could complicate ethical compliance.

name: Regulatory Compliance Frequency
consequences: Increasing audit frequency for data handling protocols reduces compliance risk but requires dedicated staff time that could otherwise support research operations.
options: Implement real-time compliance monitoring systems
Conduct quarterly third-party audits
Develop internal compliance training modules
review: Frequent audits enhance regulatory adherence but divert resources from core research activities, creating a trade-off between oversight and productivity.

name: Facility Utilization Optimization
consequences: Adjusting occupancy rates to match resource availability directly impacts data collection efficiency. Overloading suites risks staff burnout and safety compromises, while underutilization creates fixed-cost inefficiencies. A dynamic occupancy model could balance these but requires real-time demand forecasting infrastructure.
options: Implement a tiered occupancy system linking suite availability to real-time event capture rates
Introduce flexible stay durations with mandatory mid-stay reassessment for low-event participants
Create shared monitoring hours across suites to reduce per-participant staffing overhead
review: Tiered occupancy risks creating a two-tiered participant experience that could skew event capture rates among low-event individuals.

name: Participant Engagement Protocols
consequences: Enhancing participant motivation increases retention but requires proportional investment in relationship management. Over-engagement risks burnout, while minimal interaction may lead to higher dropout rates and less reliable self-reported data.
options: Establish a peer mentorship program connecting participants with long-term residents
Implement biweekly feedback loops with clinical psychologists to address procedural concerns
Create a participatory data interpretation workshop series for high-engagement individuals
review: Peer mentorship could introduce selection bias if only highly motivated participants volunteer for mentor roles.

name: Sensor Calibration Frequency
consequences: More frequent calibration improves data accuracy but increases maintenance workload and potential participant disruption. Less frequent calibration risks data degradation that could invalidate longitudinal comparisons.
options: Deploy self-calibrating sensor arrays with automated baseline correction algorithms
Schedule calibration during non-peak hours using portable diagnostic equipment
Implement event-triggered recalibration after detected anomaly patterns
review: Self-calibrating sensors may introduce unknown systematic errors if algorithmic corrections diverge from clinical standards.

name: Staff Training Modularization
consequences: Standardized training ensures consistent protocol adherence but limits adaptability to unique participant needs. Customized training improves responsiveness but creates knowledge silos and increases certification overhead.
options: Develop cross-disciplinary training modules combining sleep medicine and emergency response
Implement scenario-based drills simulating high-risk event capture situations
Create a certification ladder with progressive responsibility based on experience metrics
review: Scenario-based drills may prioritize rare emergencies over routine monitoring tasks, creating skill imbalance in daily operations.

name: Data Anonymization Thresholds
consequences: Stricter anonymization protects privacy but reduces data utility for longitudinal pattern analysis. More permissive thresholds increase re-identification risks and regulatory scrutiny.
options: Apply dynamic anonymization parameters based on participant risk profiles
Implement contextual de-identification where video data is only linked to physiological metrics in secure environments
Create synthetic data pools for algorithm training without exposing real participant records
review: Dynamic anonymization requires continuous risk assessment that may delay data processing pipelines critical for real-time event triage.

name: Participant Onboarding Rhythm
consequences: Accelerated onboarding increases throughput but reduces preparation quality. Slower onboarding improves compliance but limits enrollment capacity and data velocity.
options: Implement a phased onboarding process with mandatory pre-admission virtual simulations
Create a peer-led orientation program where current participants guide new arrivals
Schedule onboarding sessions during low-activity periods to minimize disruption
review: Peer-led orientations may create informal hierarchies that influence participant behavior patterns in ways difficult to measure.
